claim: Metformin reduces cancer incidence in adults without diabetes

rows.finding: In the Diabetes Prevention Program RCT of adults at high diabetes risk (non-diabetic, impaired glucose tolerance at randomization), metformin 850 mg BID did not reduce total cancer incidence vs placebo over a median 21 years (546 first cancers; HR 0.90, 95% CI 0.73-1.10).
rows.integrity_note: No retraction or expression of concern (verified). Trial = NCT00004992 (DPP/DPPOS), enrollment 3,234, confirmed on ClinicalTrials.gov. Only bundle row with a true non-diabetic population and RCT-tier design — load-bearing for the verdict.

rows.finding: Collaborative meta-analysis of randomized trials found no reduction in cancer with metformin (summary RR 1.02, 95% CI 0.82-1.26), directly refuting the ~one-third reduction seen in observational studies.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction/EoC (verified). Trials mostly enrolled diabetic patients, so population match to non-diabetic adults is only partial — honestly flagged false.

rows.finding: Emulating a target trial removed the apparent protective signal: primary 6-year cancer risk difference (metformin vs no metformin, in individuals WITH diabetes) was ~0 (ITT -0.2%, 95% CI -1.6% to 1.3%); a secondary emulation regardless of diabetes status was also near-zero, whereas naive observational methods appeared strongly protective.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction/EoC (verified). CORRECTED population_match true->false: the headline emulation is restricted to individuals with diabetes; only a secondary analysis is diabetes-agnostic. Explicitly shows the observational protective signal is an analytic artifact.

rows.finding: Meta-analysis of 6 RCTs found no significant association between metformin and skin cancer (melanoma OR 0.82, 0.27-2.43; total skin cancer OR 0.71, 0.42-1.20); parallel cohort meta-analysis also null.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction/EoC (verified). Diabetes/prediabetes populations; site-specific (skin), so population_match false.

rows.finding: The naive observational signal: pooled all-cancer incidence RR 0.67 (95% CI 0.53-0.85) favoring metformin, but derived mainly from cohort/case-control studies in diabetic patients; authors themselves flag need for RCTs.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction/EoC (verified). Represents the confounded observational signal later refuted by RCTs/TTE; diabetic population only, so population_match false. Normalized to 'systematic review' (pools observational data, not RCTs).

rows.finding: Observational meta-analysis reporting reduced pancreatic cancer risk with metformin (RR 0.63, 95% CI 0.46-0.86) in type 2 diabetes — a site-specific instance of the same confounded observational signal, from cohort/case-control data only.
rows.integrity_note: No retraction/EoC (verified). Purely observational; diabetic population; susceptible to time-related/immortal-time bias. Normalized to 'systematic review' (pools observational data, not RCTs).

provenance: Gathered in-window from PubMed/ClinicalTrials.gov (public). PMIDs/NCTs/DOIs only; no Consensus output redistributed.
